companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
This U.S. wholesale health-supply distributor is one of three such companies in the top 40 of the Global 500. Its revenue rose 11.6% last year, to $181 billion.

  • Ongoing litigation issues over the alleged role of Cardinal and other pharmaceutical distributors in the opioid crisis bled into the company’s 2022 financials; the company registered a $933 million loss in the fiscal year ended June 2022. But the company’s stock soared in calendar 2022, reflecting investors’ relief after Cardinal reached settlements in several opioid-related lawsuits. (The company did not admit wrongdoing in those settlements.)

  • The pharmaceutical arm of the company performed well, with a 5% increase in profit year over year.

  • CEO Mike Kaufmann was succeeded by former CFO Jason Hollar in September 2022.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Despite bringing in over $160 billion in revenue in 2021, Cardinal Health reported net income of just $611 million for the year. Litigation costs were one factor: One of several companies entangled in lawsuits over their alleged role in the opioid crisis, Cardinal in July 2021 agreed to pay $6.4 billion in settlements to help fund health care and drug-treatment programs. The company also agreed to settle a case with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission involving racial harassment claims made by Black employees at one of its distribution centers, offering $1.45 million in settlements and agreeing to implement a range of policy changes. On the business-building front, Cardinal partnered with logistics startup Zipline to deliver products to pharmacies using autonomous aircraft.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The drug and medical supply company saw 5.1% sales growth last year (its fiscal year ended in June 2020) owing to the strength of its pharmaceutical distribution business. That was particularly true during the first half of 2020, as customers stocked up on medications at the onset of the pandemic. A manufacturer and distributor of the personal protective equipment that has been much in demand, Cardinal has seen both sales of these products and the cost of making and sourcing them increase in the past year. As with other drug wholesalers, Cardinal faces legal challenges over its alleged role in America’s opioid epidemic.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The Ohio-based drug wholesaler, which counts CVS Health and Kroger as customers, saw revenues rise 6.4% in its 2019 fiscal year due to growth in its drug and specialty pharmaceutical distribution business—and despite the 2018 divestiture of part of its business in China. While depressed prices of generic medications and the cost of opioid-related litigation weighed on Cardinal’s bottom line, the company’s profits rebounded from 2018, when the company took a $1.4 billion impairment charge. Like its two large competitors, Cardinal faces thousands of lawsuits over its alleged role in the nation’s opioid epidemic. In February, states rejected a proposed $18 billion settlement with the nation’s three largest drug distributors.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
